938	## 3. Step results and disposition
939	
940	A step returns its results in the core algebra of
941	[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
942	performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
943	and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
944	admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
945	questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
946	refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
947	predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
948	core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
949	`satisfied` counts toward another predicate
950	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
951	Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
952	stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
953	read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
954	acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.
955	
956	| Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |
957	|---|---|---|
958	| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
959	| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
960	| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
961	| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
962	| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |
963	
964	A profile that refines these values for its own units maps each of its
965	values to exactly one core value under FOUNDATIONS §4 Results and adds no
966	core value.
967	
968	### Admission and activation
969	
970	A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its
971	frame is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of
972	admission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the
973	predicate "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact
974	subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for
975	the basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
976	refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
977	which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
978	this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with
979	the value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and
980	maps none of them again:
981	
982	| Outcome | Cause | Core value |
983	|---|---|---|
984	| `activated` | the contract is admitted with its admission evidence (§1), Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis and the scope are exact and the material closure is finite and unique (§2, step 1), its projection returns a selected context (§2, step 2), and activation returns `activated_frame` | satisfied |
985	| `admission_refused(authority)` | the work authority the step needs is not admitted: no admission mechanism or explicit human override admits the exact contract, or no durable result and evidence surface is authorised and available; the outcome names the missing authority or surface and its owner | out_of_frame |
986	| `admission_refused(basis)` | the contract's cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis, or the exact subject and basis it names, cannot support it; the outcome names that basis | invalid_basis |
987	| `closure_unresolved` | the seed set Z, the relation family R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not exact, or the material closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis (§2, step 1; AC-010), or the projection of the closure returns a gap or refusal (§2, step 2; AC-011); the outcome names the condition that fails and the basis coordinates that leave it open | invalid_basis |
988	| `out_of_frame` | no available frame and actor pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs (§2, Activation), or no fit option of §2 step 3 fits the selected context to an actor's envelope | out_of_frame |
989	| `activation_refusal` with its cause | a cause REFERENCE_FRAME §5 states | the core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 maps that cause to |
990	
991	These outcomes are not values of construction availability and are not
992	results of a step. A refused admission or activation creates no step, no
993	activation of the step's frame and no work result, the closed output of a
994	constructing actor to its consumer; the outcome returns to the assigning
995	authority or the declared result carrier, and no consumer records it as a
996	step's stop state. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §5](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#work-result)
997	applies this rule to the Worker.
998	Purpose and material relation: a mismatch known before the step begins is
999	reported with its cause in the one core, so it is neither mistaken for a
1000	step that stopped nor for one that ran.
1001	
1002	### Construction availability
1003	
1004	A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
1005	constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
1006	assessing step. Construction availability records whether that output
1007	exists (P5, P6):
1008	
1009	| Value | Core value | Ground |
1010	|---|---|---|
1011	| `candidate_ready` | satisfied | an exact candidate and its transition evidence are available |
1012	| `refused` | falsified | lawful activation occurred, and a governing prohibition or an owner-valid construction refusal defeats the requested construction; the prohibition or refusal is the counterexample |
1013	| `incomplete` | falsified | the lawfully activated step stopped without its output, because an evaluation the output needs was not performed or could not be decided on the admissible evidence, or bounded execution ended first; the stop basis is the counterexample, and it and the residuals name which |
1014	| `re_entry_requested(authority)` | out_of_frame | a material decision the step needs lies outside its grant; the value names the owner of that decision |
1015	| `re_entry_requested(basis)` | invalid_basis | the activated basis can no longer support the work |
1016	
1017	The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation: the cause of
1018	the stop selects the value, and payload wording, stop timing or actor
1019	preference cannot select another. A mismatch known during admission or
1020	activation is no value of this refinement, because no step exists; it
1021	takes its outcome under Admission and activation above.
1022	
1023	`satisfied` here establishes availability only and never counts toward the
1024	candidate's fitness or acceptance (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).
1025	
1026	`incomplete` maps to `falsified` only for "a candidate is available", never
1027	to `indeterminate`. The step's evaluations keep their own results: each
1028	evaluation it performed returns its core value, `indeterminate` where the
1029	admissible evidence could not decide; each evaluation it planned and did
1030	not perform has no result, and its work state (§5) carries it as a
1031	residual with the capability or the execution left unfinished
1032	(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, the third case of the boundary). An evaluation
1033	not performed thus stays distinct from one whose evidence cannot decide
1034	(P5, P6).
1035	
1036	An assessing step that ends `incomplete` leaves each criterion it did not
1037	evaluate not performed: no result, never `falsified`. The `falsified` of its
1038	availability concerns its own output, never the subject under assessment
1039	(P6).
1040	
1041	The cause of a re-entry request is part of its value, because a re-entry
1042	request without its cause would map to `out_of_frame` or to
1043	`invalid_basis` according to that cause, and a refined value maps to
1044	exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Refinements). A stop
1045	with both causes records both and takes `re_entry_requested(basis)`,
1046	because a decision cannot be taken on a basis that cannot support it (P5,
1047	P3).
1048	
1049	### Disposition
1050	
1051	The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
1052	semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5). An assessor may recommend one; the
1053	recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
1054	([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
1055	acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
1056	results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
1057	to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
1058	boundary":
1059	
1060	| Disposition | Condition | Core value |
1061	|---|---|---|
1062	| `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
1063	| `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |
1064	| `re_enter` | the governing outcome, a requirement, an identity, a lifecycle, an authority, a public contract or the accepted design must change | invalid_basis |
1065	| `reject` | the candidate violates a governing relation or leaves an undisposed competing truth path | falsified |
1066	
1067	For `local_repair` the local defect, and for `reject` the violated relation
1068	or the competing truth path, is the counterexample to accepting this
1069	candidate; a repaired candidate is a new candidate with its own results.
1070	For `re_enter` the governing basis the candidate was built and assessed on
1071	must change, so that basis cannot support acceptance; the change re-enters
1072	at its owning relation (§4). The core values place
1073	acceptance in the one core, as FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires, so that a
1074	consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
1075	acceptance (P6).
1076	
1077	Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
1078	bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every
1079	local action (P4b). Repeated rejection against one unchanged boundary
1080	requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
1081	components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
1082	sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
1083	review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an
1084	unchanged failed construction relation as if iteration alone could close
1085	it (P2).
1086	
1087	### Ambiguity outcome
1088	
1089	A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
1090	outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
1091	[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
1092	applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
1093	maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
1094	the exact basis" (P5, P6):
1095	
1096	| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
1097	|---|---|---|
1098	| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
1099	| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
1100	| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
1101	| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |
1102	
1103	An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
1104	`blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
1105	evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
1106	the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
1107	the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
1108	Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
1109	dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
1110	as if it were resolved. The mapping places ambiguity outcomes
1111	in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
1112	(P5, P6).
1113	
1114	### Effects
1115	
1116	An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
1117	mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
1118	declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
1119	admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
1120	premise, P6):
1121	
1122	| Value | Core value | Ground |
1123	|---|---|---|
1124	| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
1125	| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
1126	| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |
1127	
1128	`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
1129	absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
1130	not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
1131	`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.
1132	
1133	Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
1134	above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
1135	effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
1136	that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
1137	effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
1138	established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
1139	the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
1140	`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
1141	the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
1142	`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
1143	not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
1144	the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
1145	counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
1146	success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
1147	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).
1148	
1149	An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
1150	`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
1151	established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
1152	action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
1153	value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
1154	while its end is not established.
1155	
1156	The refinement's material relation is whether an action whose
1157	external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
1158	lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
1159	this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
1160	effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
1161	counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
1162	effect that may still be acting.
1163

at its owning relation (§4). The core values place
acceptance in the one core, as FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires, so that a
consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
acceptance (P6).

Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every
local action (P4b). Repeated rejection against one unchanged boundary
requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an
unchanged failed construction relation as if iteration alone could close
it (P2).

### Ambiguity outcome

A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |

An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
`blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
as if it were resolved. The mapping places ambiguity outcomes
in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
(P5, P6).

### Effects

An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

| Value | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |

`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.

Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
while its end is not established.

The refinement's material relation is whether an action whose
external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
effect that may still be acting.

1458	### The workspace and an actor's account
1459	
1460	The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
1461	are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
1462	material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
1463	context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
1464	projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
1465	correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
1466	step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
1467	never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
1468	actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
1469	it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).
1470	
1471	Acquisition ([§2](#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)) observes the
1472	current subject and its authoritative inputs. Where they materially
1473	disagree with a cached belief, a retained summary or a prior result, the
1474	actor reconciles the disagreement: current evidence corrects the account,
1475	and what the evidence cannot decide stays an explicit unknown. A stored
1476	belief, a summary or a successful prior result never overrules contrary
1477	current evidence. A prior result is relied on only after its
1478	applicability and invalidators are checked against the current subject
1479	and inputs (§7). The actor corrects its account within its grant; where
1480	resolving the disagreement needs an operation, a territory or a decision
1481	outside the grant, the step stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`,
1482	naming the owner of what it needs (§3 Construction availability) (P5,
1483	P6).
1484	
1485	Discarding an actor's private context resets nothing: the workspace, the
1486	applicable valid work and the outstanding obligations remain as the work
1487	state records them. A missing trace in a context, a memory or a summary is
1488	no evidence about the subject. It shows neither that work was not done
1489	nor that an external effect did not occur, nor that it ended; an effect
1490	of uncertain completion keeps the value `completion_unknown`, or its end
1491	stays not established beside its `not_effected` value, until evidence
1492	about the subject decides it (§3 Effects) (P5).
1493	
1494	Work that an interruption left partly written is part of the current
1495	material state from which resumption (above) starts, and is assessed as
1496	it stands; an assessment that was not performed has no result and is
1497	never recorded as performed
1498	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); §3 Construction
1499	availability). The method imposes no universal reset and no obligation to
1500	replay the complete history. The recovery contract that applies, which is
1501	the resuming step's intake with the work state, determines which
1502	observations and which effect reconciliations the next dependent action
1503	needs. Handoff between actors is by closed results, which carry no private
1504	working context and keep their validity and independence conditions (§7)
1505	(P0, P4b).
1506	
1507	Purpose and material relation: finite context (P0) means an actor's
1508	context ends or is replaced while the work continues, and discarding it is
1509	safe only because the step-produced facts the outer contract needs are
1510	recorded (P4b). Treating the account as the truth surface would let a
1511	stale account overrule the workspace; treating a discarded account as a
1512	reset would erase progress or repeat an effect that occurred (P5, P6). The
1513	material relation is whether a decision relies on an account that current
1514	evidence contradicts, or reads a missing record as undone work or an
1515	absent effect.  The workspace, the
1516	work state and the closed results carry it, and no further carrier is
1517	required.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

### The workspace and an actor's account

The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).

Acquisition ([§2](#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)) observes the
current subject and its authoritative inputs. Where they materially
disagree with a cached belief, a retained summary or a prior result, the
actor reconciles the disagreement: current evidence corrects the account,
and what the evidence cannot decide stays an explicit unknown. A stored
belief, a summary or a successful prior result never overrules contrary
current evidence. A prior result is relied on only after its
applicability and invalidators are checked against the current subject
and inputs (§7). The actor corrects its account within its grant; where
resolving the disagreement needs an operation, a territory or a decision
outside the grant, the step stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`,
naming the owner of what it needs (§3 Construction availability) (P5,
P6).

Discarding an actor's private context resets nothing: the workspace, the
applicable valid work and the outstanding obligations remain as the work
state records them. A missing trace in a context, a memory or a summary is
no evidence about the subject. It shows neither that work was not done
nor that an external effect did not occur, nor that it ended; an effect
of uncertain completion keeps the value `completion_unknown`, or its end
stays not established beside its `not_effected` value, until evidence
about the subject decides it (§3 Effects) (P5).

Work that an interruption left partly written is part of the current
material state from which resumption (above) starts, and is assessed as
it stands; an assessment that was not performed has no result and is
never recorded as performed
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); §3 Construction
availability). The method imposes no universal reset and no obligation to
replay the complete history. The recovery contract that applies, which is
the resuming step's intake with the work state, determines which
observations and which effect reconciliations the next dependent action
needs. Handoff between actors is by closed results, which carry no private
working context and keep their validity and independence conditions (§7)
(P0, P4b).

Purpose and material relation: finite context (P0) means an actor's
context ends or is replaced while the work continues, and discarding it is
safe only because the step-produced facts the outer contract needs are
recorded (P4b). Treating the account as the truth surface would let a
stale account overrule the workspace; treating a discarded account as a
reset would erase progress or repeat an effect that occurred (P5, P6). The
material relation is whether a decision relies on an account that current
evidence contradicts, or reads a missing record as undone work or an
absent effect.  The workspace, the
work state and the closed results carry it, and no further carrier is
required.

## 7. Closed result and reuse

A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is

transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
permission (P4b, P0).

The sufficiency of a handed-off result or reference for subsequent decisions
is [FOUNDATIONS §4 Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)'s
consumer-relative claim. Reuse preserves the material standing and
continuation distinctions, including unassessed versus indeterminate; a
role change alone requires no full-history scan or new representation.

The selection of affected results after a change and the conditions for
retaining evidence on a new subject are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse);
this section applies them to closed results and handoffs, and the three
invalidators below are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected
when its dependencies `D*(t)` meet the impact cover `I(Δ)` (P3, P6).

A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
results. Invalidation withdraws the result from direct reliance; whether
its evidence is retained on the new basis is decided by `retain_applicable`
of FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse, and the changed
coordinate alone establishes neither that the claim fails nor that it
holds. The invalidators are three:

- a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
  input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
  predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
  change when it is material to the result as
  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
  when it could change the result's value;
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

A changed source, task or actor condition is a changed basis where the
basis binds it, and otherwise a material input change; a role change that
alters a required actor condition is such a change, while a role,
conversation or resumption change that alters none of these invalidates
nothing (P3, P6).

Judgment continuity names the basis and the evidence; Return A Closed
Result names inputs and the observation. A member, profile or project
that names a trigger for its own domain, such as a changed projection,
rule or configuration, names it as an instance of one of these three and
states no parallel list (P3, P4b, P6). A reused judgment does not
satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor
acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment. [TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity)
uses the same evidence invalidator. Naming these kinds once gives every
consumer the same triggers. The
material relation is whether a result is relied on after a change that
could alter it (P3, P6). Whether a revision of a frame needs a new
revision coordinate is
[REFERENCE_FRAME §10](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#revision-actions)'s question;
whether a result it touches stays valid is this section's.

### Transition evidence

A reviewable transition identifies the exact candidate, the affected
relations, the changed realisation paths, the authority paths added or
removed, the retained and open seams, the focused proof, any required
integration proof, the explicit non-changes, and, where an assessor was
activated, the assessor's recommended disposition, with the decision
owner's disposition beside it once one is made (§3). Consumers
choose the representation. Transition evidence is a read

1132	## 12. Complete engagement transition
1133	
1134	The steps below describe the coordinated branch selected under §3. Direct
1135	Worker engagement keeps the same sufficient intake, work-result algebra,
1136	closure conditions and owner boundaries without inserting an Executive
1137	appointment, or a review that no applicable condition requires (P0, P6).
1138	
1139	### 1. Existing authority selects the basis
1140	
1141	Goals, Product, requirements, accepted design, a ticket, release law or an
1142	admitted bounded proxy selects the outcome and the work authority under its
1143	existing owner. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis
1144	(PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7) projects that decision (P6).
1145	
1146	### 2. Executive activates Worker
1147	
1148	In the coordinated branch the Executive applies `activate` (REFERENCE_FRAME
1149	§5) to the sufficient execution intake of ACTIVATION §1. The packet is
1150	REFERENCE_FRAME §11; for this step it identifies (P0, P6):
1151	
1152	- the selected complete method and project authority;
1153	- the exact governed outcome and checkpoint;
1154	- the affected causal relation set and the governing invariants;
1155	- the selected computational relations and specialist frames;
1156	- where testing evidence is required: the testing claims, exact subjects,
1157	  frame topology, material combination populations, ordinary paths,
1158	  oracles and forbidden-path exclusions (ASSURANCE §7 to §9);
1159	- the Worker's authority and capability envelope, and, where mutation is
1160	  authorised, the exact inherited operation grant, subject and write
1161	  territory;
1162	- the evidence and qualification obligations;
1163	- exclusions, prohibited competing paths, stop conditions and re-entry
1164	  conditions; and
1165	- the exact bounded action already authorised.
1166	
1167	If activation detects a known capability, authority, subject, basis or
1168	topology mismatch, it returns `activation_refusal` directly to the
1169	Executive, with the cause and core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives it. No
1170	Worker frame is active, no Worker evaluation occurs, and the
1171	Executive does not manufacture a Worker result to represent the failed
1172	activation (P5, P6).
1173	
1174	### 3. Worker returns to Executive
1175	
1176	Every coordinated Worker activation ends in one closed work result sent to
1177	the Executive; direct work uses its declared result consumer (P5, P6):
1178	
1179	```text
1180	WorkerResult
1181	  = candidate_ready(exact_subject, transition_evidence, residuals)
1182	  | refused(reason, authority, evidence)
1183	  | incomplete(residuals, evidence, stop_basis)
1184	  | re_entry_requested(owner, material_relation, evidence)
1185	```
1186	
1187	The notation explains and mandates no schema. The material relation of
1188	`re_entry_requested` names its cause, authority or basis, which is part of
1189	the value. Each value maps to exactly one core value for "a candidate is
1190	available" under
1191	[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability),
1192	read as in §5 Work result; the mapping applies only after lawful
1193	activation. The Worker does not send a candidate directly into an
1194	implicitly active Reviewer. It stops after returning the result (P5,
1195	P6).
1196	
1197	### 4. Executive evaluates the work result
1198	
1199	For `refused`, `incomplete` or `re_entry_requested`, the Executive verifies
1200	the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation. It records the
1201	applicable disposition, or reactivates work only where current authority
1202	already permits that action. None of these variants is accepted progress
1203	because work occurred (P6, P5).
1204	
1205	Whatever the variant, an effect of uncertain completion, one the work
1206	result names `completion_unknown` or names `not_effected` with its end not
1207	established ([ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects)), is
1208	reconciled under
1209	[ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart), sufficiently for
1210	the next dependent action, before work is reactivated, the effect is
1211	repeated or any action that depends on it is taken (P5, P6).
1212	
1213	For `candidate_ready`, the Executive verifies the exact subject and decides
1214	whether independent assessment is required. It applies the boundaries at
1215	which this method requires it,
1216	[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
1217	the execution relation's assessment where required (ACTIVATION §1); method
1218	qualification ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method));
1219	and the further boundaries the governing basis adds, as
1220	[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) permits: Product,
1221	release, risk or the admitted work contract. What counts as independent is
1222	EVALUATION §3's. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a
1223	required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit or negative-path
1224	result is missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material
1225	frame result (P6; ASSURANCE §10).
1226	
1227	### 5A. Candidate does not require independent review

## 12. Complete engagement transition

The steps below describe the coordinated branch selected under §3. Direct
Worker engagement keeps the same sufficient intake, work-result algebra,
closure conditions and owner boundaries without inserting an Executive
appointment, or a review that no applicable condition requires (P0, P6).

### 1. Existing authority selects the basis

Goals, Product, requirements, accepted design, a ticket, release law or an
admitted bounded proxy selects the outcome and the work authority under its
existing owner. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis
(PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7) projects that decision (P6).

### 2. Executive activates Worker

In the coordinated branch the Executive applies `activate` (REFERENCE_FRAME
§5) to the sufficient execution intake of ACTIVATION §1. The packet is
REFERENCE_FRAME §11; for this step it identifies (P0, P6):

- the selected complete method and project authority;
- the exact governed outcome and checkpoint;
- the affected causal relation set and the governing invariants;
- the selected computational relations and specialist frames;
- where testing evidence is required: the testing claims, exact subjects,
  frame topology, material combination populations, ordinary paths,
  oracles and forbidden-path exclusions (ASSURANCE §7 to §9);
- the Worker's authority and capability envelope, and, where mutation is
  authorised, the exact inherited operation grant, subject and write
  territory;
- the evidence and qualification obligations;
- exclusions, prohibited competing paths, stop conditions and re-entry
  conditions; and
- the exact bounded action already authorised.

If activation detects a known capability, authority, subject, basis or
topology mismatch, it returns `activation_refusal` directly to the
Executive, with the cause and core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives it. No
Worker frame is active, no Worker evaluation occurs, and the
Executive does not manufacture a Worker result to represent the failed
activation (P5, P6).

### 3. Worker returns to Executive

Every coordinated Worker activation ends in one closed work result sent to
the Executive; direct work uses its declared result consumer (P5, P6):

```text
WorkerResult
  = candidate_ready(exact_subject, transition_evidence, residuals)
  | refused(reason, authority, evidence)
  | incomplete(residuals, evidence, stop_basis)
  | re_entry_requested(owner, material_relation, evidence)
```

The notation explains and mandates no schema. The material relation of
`re_entry_requested` names its cause, authority or basis, which is part of
the value. Each value maps to exactly one core value for "a candidate is
available" under
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability),
read as in §5 Work result; the mapping applies only after lawful
activation. The Worker does not send a candidate directly into an
implicitly active Reviewer. It stops after returning the result (P5,
P6).

### 4. Executive evaluates the work result

For `refused`, `incomplete` or `re_entry_requested`, the Executive verifies
the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation. It records the
applicable disposition, or reactivates work only where current authority
already permits that action. None of these variants is accepted progress
because work occurred (P6, P5).

Whatever the variant, an effect of uncertain completion, one the work
result names `completion_unknown` or names `not_effected` with its end not
established ([ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects)), is
reconciled under
[ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart), sufficiently for
the next dependent action, before work is reactivated, the effect is
repeated or any action that depends on it is taken (P5, P6).

For `candidate_ready`, the Executive verifies the exact subject and decides
whether independent assessment is required. It applies the boundaries at
which this method requires it,
[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
the execution relation's assessment where required (ACTIVATION §1); method
qualification ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method));
and the further boundaries the governing basis adds, as
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) permits: Product,
release, risk or the admitted work contract. What counts as independent is
EVALUATION §3's. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a
required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit or negative-path
result is missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material
frame result (P6; ASSURANCE §10).

### 5A. Candidate does not require independent review

In the coordinated branch, when independent review is not required, the
Executive consumes the exact candidate, the Worker's self-review, the
transition evidence and any mandatory specialist results, and applies the
disposition within its decision envelope. Self-review stays Worker
evidence; the disposition does not relabel it as independent (P6).

Its family table, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,
in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's
consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the
family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).
Purpose and material relation:
each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,
so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a
profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).

A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test
subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by
precedent.

## 2. Graph execution

Graph execution is two tier-3 members, indexed here; each states its
law in full and declares its bindings under §1 (P0 boundary, P1):

| Member | Binds or adds |
|---|---|
| [ODD](ODD.md) | the bounded step of FOUNDATIONS P0 to one vector or edge traversal and common F_D through an exact-edition import with separate operation profiles, and graph-native F_P and F_H as declared specialisations of SPEC_METHOD §5 ([§5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute)); the refinement of ACTIVATION §4 to graph functions, with the cumulative environment law of §11.8 declared as its specialised contract for carrying earlier outputs ([§5 Graph functions](ODD.md#graph-functions), [§11.8](ODD.md#118-cumulative-environment-law-is-mandatory)) |
| [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md) | an optional closed model-family signature over one exact `a_c` basis of AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS for immutable occurrence histories over a mutable subject, with OP-001 to OP-007 |

The ownership split of graph execution (runtime, product, service layers)
is [ODD §10](ODD.md#10-what-an-odd-product-is); the worker's internal
solution strategy stays outside the framework under
[ODD §5](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute). Where another member says that
this section keeps the ODD binding, the binding is the one ODD states and
this section indexes (P0, P1).

## 3. Software design

[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md) is the software-design profile. It
imports the core and binds: ontology-first derivation of operation
identities from discovered functionality through logical completeness,
Prime contraction, the irreducible architectural carrier set and its
projections; proportional design sequencing with the decision-complete
design gate; bounded frame conservation; native constructability;
capability and foundation selection; transformation admission
completeness; invariant reconstruction sufficiency; computational
realisation projection; the module taxonomy and realisation rules; and
the design review questions and checklist. Its design-to-module evidence
route, module-derived unit tests and module lifecycle confirmation are
ASSURANCE §14 to §16, and its core rule and non-goals SPEC_METHOD §2
Realisation shape. The per-boundary cost of the derivation chain is
decided there (DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing, §7 Gate
and retrospective work) (P2, P0).

## 4. UX

[UX](UX.md) is the UX profile. It refines DESIGN_MODULE for modules that
realise a UX surface, imports the core, and binds: the Elm process model
with typed State, Msg, Update, View, Cmd and Sub; the boundary between UX
messages and admitted product carriers; the state transition law; the
effect membrane; binding to AssetSurface or an equivalent typed contract;
view continuation and the Msg-replay proof; view shape; type sharing with
runtime validation at untrusted seams; the accessibility minimum;
realisation discretion; adoption with the scaffold and exemption law and
UX sprint compliance escrow; the failure patterns and review questions;
and its refinements of the core result algebra, each value mapped to one
core value (UX §15). Its binding of TICKETS §3's generalised escrow terms
is declared in its lead (P6, P2).

## 5. World model

[WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md) is the world-model profile. It imports the
core and binds: the imported product-lineage concepts and the Builder
Project specialisation; the Markov-object construct at candidate status
with its effective blanket, working refinements, epistemic status and
promotion gate; the core claims and units; entity recovery and the entity
cut as the published identity-bearing unit, with its admissibility,
discrimination and publication law; the attribute ledger; the
representation, materialisation and publication laws; Markov-object
overlay construction; saturation; composition of local artifacts;
projection; the control and data planes; the proof law and
world-model-driven development; and its refinements of the core result
algebra, each value mapped to one core value (WORLD_MODEL §14). Its
binding of FOUNDATIONS §2 Object
and P3's boundary claim to the entity cut is declared in its lead.
Nothing in the core depends on the construct being established (P3, P6).

## 6. Engagement baseline

[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) is the optional
engagement-baseline profile. It imports the core and describes the
executive configuration, one configuration in the sense of
[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), with three
engagement frames (Executive, Worker, Reviewer) and a catalogue of
specialist frames, mapped onto the law of tiers 1 and 2. Its frame names
bind the responsibilities that configuration allocates under
[ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation),
not roles imported by spelling, as its lead declares (P1, P6).

724	rule. Purpose and material relation: these admission conditions govern every

727	durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and

731	the missing work authority without execution, as `admission_refused` with
732	its cause ([§3 Admission and activation](../ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation)).

734	is owned by [TICKETS §5](../TICKETS.md#5-from-carrier-to-execution).

contract stays drafted or rejected, and prose asserting admission is not
admission evidence (P6; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution
basis). Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome,
prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and
drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority
its owner has not admitted (P6, P2;
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](../FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
creates no authority). Only an admitted contract activates a step: no
result, child completion, tool output, model response, shared actor or
lateral handoff activates another step or authorises continuation by
itself, and a profile that routes results names its instances of this
rule. Purpose and material relation: these admission conditions govern every
configuration, and their generic owner is this section (P6).
The admitted contract names one
durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and
residual obligation is recorded there before return, a conversation return
alone is not durable evidence, and if no such surface is authorised and
available, admission refuses (P4b). Absent or rejected admission returns
the missing work authority without execution, as `admission_refused` with
its cause ([§3 Admission and activation](../ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation)).
The selection of the carrier (ticket, sprint entry, run-scoped contract)
is owned by [TICKETS §5](../TICKETS.md#5-from-carrier-to-execution).
